identification.summary: RaHDit (Russian Angry Hackers Did It) is a pro-Kremlin hacktivist group that, per OFAC as relayed by secondary reporting, is allegedly composed of active and former Russian intelligence officers [S1][S2]. Russian media reported in July 2022 that the group published data on about 1,000 Ukrainian intelligence employees [S4].
identification.firstObserved: 2022-07 or earlier (earliest cited report: Izvestia, 2022-07-06, on a data release about Ukrainian intelligence staff; search snippets suggest earlier releases in June 2022 that are not cited here) [S4].
identification.notes: Secondary sources say OFAC designated the group's head, Aleksey Garashchenko, on 2024-09-04 [S1][S2][S3]. The NemeZida site name and the Kursk-related leak figures come from undated or non-primary pages that are not cited here; see gaps.

attribution.confidence: Treasury (via secondary reporting) described RaHDit as allegedly made up of active and former Russian intelligence officers and said Garashchenko works directly with Russian intelligence, Presidential Administration members and RT employees [S1][S2]. This is a US government allegation reported second-hand; the primary Treasury release was not opened.
attribution.basis: OFAC designation of Aleksey Garashchenko, Anastasia Yermoshkina and Aleksandr Nezhentsev on 2024-09-04 as reported by law-firm and trade press [S1][S2][S3].

targeting.notes: Only the 2022 Izvestia report of a data release on Ukrainian intelligence employees is cited here [S4]; this is Russian media and may reflect the group's own claims.

capabilities.summary: Hack-and-leak style publication of personal data on Ukrainian intelligence personnel was reported by Russian media in 2022 [S4]. No technical tooling, intrusion methods or infrastructure are documented in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Release of data on Ukrainian intelligence staff
campaigns.summary: Izvestia reported that RaHDit published data on about 1,000 Ukrainian intelligence employees (per the article headline); reporting is Russian media and unverified [S4].

campaigns.name: OFAC designation of RaHDit leadership
campaigns.summary: Treasury sanctioned Garashchenko, Yermoshkina and Nezhentsev alongside RT and Dialog-related designations in a response to Russian election influence efforts, per secondary reporting [S1][S2][S3].

diamond.adversary: Group allegedly led by Aleksey Garashchenko, described by OFAC as working with Russian intelligence, the Presidential Administration and RT staff [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Alignment with Russian influence operations, per OFAC's description of Garashchenko's work with RT and the Presidential Administration [S1][S2].

gaps: Primary Treasury/OFAC press release, State Department Rewards for Justice notice (a reported offer of up to $10 million for information on RaHDit) and any DOJ material were not opened; WebFetch failed with DNS errors for all hosts, so only search-result summaries were available.

Undated or non-primary pages seen but not cited for lack of a verifiable date: Malpedia, GlobalSecurity, Strobes, Cyclowiki, lentepubblica.it (claims of 800+ Ukrainian personnel tied to Kursk, 1,500 SVR staff, 755 defaced government sites), Lenta, RBC. These figures are unverified.
The existing Flashpoint (pro-Kremlin hacktivist groups) and Risky Business (Doppelganger) leads in the actor record were not readable this session.
No technical analysis (initial access, malware, infrastructure) from a Western vendor was found; whether the group actually performed intrusions or republished data from others is unknown.
Group claims of providing intelligence to the Russian army and ties to other hacktivist groups are unverified.
No MITRE group ID or Microsoft name known; vendor cluster overlaps unknown.
